QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_75

question.text: Bharat Asset Management's MF-for-SSE scheme funds an SE that delivers BOTH environmental restoration and financial inclusion outcomes addressed by different SAS thematic areas. When the SIA reports impact across these dimensions (including any monetary metric), the SIA should:

answer.text: Select and disclose standard-specific indicators for each thematic area, disclose the calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations underlying any monetary metric, and avoid presenting a single aggregate figure that over-compares unlike measures
Sum any monetary indicators across the two standards into a single ratio without further disclosure
Pick the higher monetary indicator and report only that
Report no monetary or thematic indicators

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook expects the SIA to select indicators specific to each applicable SAS thematic area and, where monetary approaches are used, to disclose the underlying calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations. It also cautions that there are no common measures across dimensions, so collapsing different standards into a single comparable number can mislead Report users. The right practice is to report each standard's indicators separately with clear disclosure of method. The Trap: Option B masks methodological differences and lacks the required disclosure. Option C cherry-picks. Option D unjustifiably omits useful information that the workbook expects the SIA to present. Note: When indicators are monetary, the workbook is explicit that the SIA must disclose the calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations behind them. Aggregation across unlike measures should be avoided or clearly qualified.
